text: Carriers are useless without ground forces to fill them, and ground forces are stuck without carriers to move them: build the two together.
why: Reviewed games had the agent build empty carriers, and infantry at home with nothing to carry it, so neither took planets.

text: Don't spend the planets or trade goods an objective needs before the status phase: exhausting a planet for a build, a secondary or Leadership spends it for the round.
why: The agent spent the resources or influence it needed for a spend objective during the action phase and could not score it.

text: A planet with no ground forces falls to anyone who lands: leave infantry on planets an enemy ship can reach, or accept the risk knowingly.
why: Planets the agent left bare were taken by neighbours who simply landed on them.

text: Never let the player holding Mecatol Rex take Imperial: its primary scores a public objective and gives a victory point for holding Mecatol. Take Imperial yourself or pick so they cannot get it.
why: In reviewed games the agent left Imperial to the Mecatol holder, who scored twice from it.

text: Own your slice early: the two systems in front of your home and one on either side are yours to take in the first rounds, before neighbours do.
Public objective tempo comes before secrets: score a public objective every round, and prefer secret objectives you can complete in the action phase on this board.
Warfare's primary frees a carrier to expand twice in one round: activate and land, play Warfare to take that command token back, then move the same carrier on. Bring ground forces for both systems.
Gravity rifts destroy ships that leave them on a roll of 1 to 3: moving through one risks the ships, and the ground forces aboard.
Mentak's Pillage takes trade goods from its neighbours who hold 3 or more: next to Mentak, spend trade goods or keep them below 3.
Stalling is for the late game, not the early one: an early stall wastes a tactic token you need for expansion and production. Pass if there is nothing worth doing.
Objectives scored by other players are still scorable by you: every player can score each public objective once.
why: The agent dropped plans for objectives once someone else had scored them.
